messages.msg:
Lesson 01 builds SiteHeader with a greeting (

Welcome back, {userName}

), a corner line (Signed in as {userName}), and a search box, in that order, for the user Mary. Verified in React 19.3.1 in Chrome and jsdom: with text typed in the search box, deleting the corner element and saving empties the box, because the input moves from the third place to the second and React builds a new one; {false} in the corner's place keeps the box and its text. Lesson 24 can reuse this header to show that React matches elements by type and position.

Lecture 2 shows that a component defined inside another component loses the typed text and the focus on every save, and promises that Lecture 24 explains why: React compares components by the function itself, and a nested definition is a new function on every run, so React treats it as a different component and resets its state. Please open with this case (CommentBox inside ArticleCard, 'Great news' typed, save, empty box) and cite Lecture 2.
